# Napkin Sketch Notes

**Maya Chen:** The founders had no store, no money and no jobs. What they had was a
drawing of a warehouse where every aisle looked like a lumberyard.

**Tom Okafor:** They kept coming back to one idea. Customers would come for the prices.
They would come back for the help.

Note: the napkin itself was never found.

**Maya Chen:** That is the part people forget. The orange apron was a promise that
somebody in the aisle knew how to fix your sink. It was cheaper than advertising. It
was better than advertising. It turned a warehouse into a classroom. Contractors
trusted it. Homeowners trusted it more. Within ten years the stores were full on
Saturday mornings. Within twenty the competitors were closing.
